Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: 1:02:00
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood), Daniel Cho (Redwood), Lena Ortiz (Palisade), Samir Gupta (Palisade), Nora Fields (Palisade)

Auto-summary (auto-gen):
Palisade is approaching renewal window and wants to bridge capacity while they finalize EU private deployment. Main asks: temporary capacity uplift (reserved + burst), contract amendment options, security signoff for KMS/HSM and SOC2 artifacts, and schedule for a 24h throughput benchmark on their representative traffic. SE to run tests; AE to send pricing and legal amendment.

Topics: capacity bridging, EU private deployment timeline, KMS/HSM and SOC2, throughput benchmarks, pricing amendment, SSO and RBAC mapping

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run about an hour, want to confirm agenda — renewals, a bridging capacity option for the next 60 days, and the EU private cluster updates.
[00:00:18] Lena (Palisade): yeah thanks, morning for us — um, the big thing is we need to avoid throttling during Q4 marketing push, and we still haven't finished our internal procurement for the private control plane. so short term we need headroom.
[00:00:36] Daniel (Redwood SE): quick clarifying q: when you say headroom, are you looking for a reserved committed uplift or a short burst capacity model? we can mix both.
[00:00:44] Samir (Palisade): for this push we'd prefer a hybrid — reserve some baseline but keep burst for unpredictable spikes. cost matters but availability > per-token cost for the next two months.
[00:00:56] Nora (Palisade CISO): and from security side we need docs — SOC 2 type II, KMS/HSM architecture, and SSO integration mapping. also separation of logs, audit retention.
[00:01:12] Maya: absolutely, we can send SOC2 and the KMS integration notes. Daniel, can you outline the uplift patterns we typically recommend?
[00:01:25] Daniel: sure, so option A is short-term reserved nodes — add 2x p4d-equivalent reserved slots, which gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost. option B is burst credit pool — quick to enable but less predictable latency at tail. option C is staged uplift: immediate small reserve + burst for spikes, then flip to Dedicated after EU private is live.
[00:01:50] Lena: that staged one sounds closest. timeline: EU private is targeted for mid-Nov but procurement might slip. can we bridge until the private is live?
[00:02:02] Maya: yes, that's the bridge: contract amendment to extend current term by 60 days with an uplift ramp and then a handoff clause to private deployment. i'll coordinate legal.
[00:02:15] Samir: side question on the private: will we get a private control plane with VPC peering, or is it customer-managed? we need to know for networking and firewall rules.
[00:02:28] Daniel: the model we usually do is customer-managed VPC peering plus our private control plane in their region. you can also opt for fully on-prem if needed, but that adds ops overhead.
[00:02:41] Nora: on-prem adds audit work; we prefer VPC peering and KMS integration to keep keys in our HSM. is that supported?
[00:02:51] Daniel: yes, KMS/HSM integrations are supported — we map keys for encryption-at-rest and provide guidance for key rotation. i'll include the integration notes, there are some platform-specific steps for Azure Key Vault vs AWS KMS.
[00:03:06] Maya: quick note, we do have a sample doc we can share — SOC2 redacted report, KMS architecture diagram, and a SAML SSO mapping template.
[00:03:17] Lena: great. also, what's the expected latency profile with the bridge? our SLO is 95th < 250ms for generation endpoints, is that realistic?
[00:03:28] Daniel: with reserved nodes it's achievable for most models if you pin to low-latency variants; with burst pool you may see 95th slip to ~400ms under big spikes. also depends on sequence length & KV cache hit rates — if you can supply sample traffic we can simulate.
[00:03:48] Samir: we'll share our traffic — it's heavy on 512 token completions, lots of prefix reuse, so KV cache should help.
[00:03:59] Maya: perfect, daniel will run a 24-hour synthetic throughput test using your sample. that will give concrete latency/cost numbers.
[00:04:08] Daniel: yeah i'll spin up a test run, we'll measure p50/p95/p99, token cost, and GPU utilization. note: quantization profiles may change perf/cost tradeoffs — we can try int8-ish profiles but need to validate quality.
[00:04:25] Lena: thanks, on cost front, can you show the delta between just burst vs 2x reserved vs staged? we need a clean one-page comparison for finance.
[00:04:36] Maya: we'll send a pricing delta sheet — i'll include a simple expected monthly cost and an amortized per-token estimate for each option.
[00:04:43] [00:04:47] Speaker 1 (unknown): (inaudible)
[00:04:52] Nora: one more security ask, audit logs: how long are they retained in Dedicated vs Private? we need 2 years for audit comps.
[00:05:02] Daniel: dedicated gives configurable retention — out of box it's 90 days, but with the enterprise add-on we can extend to 2 years into their SIEM via forwarding. Private gives you full control.
[00:05:15] Samir: ok can you include the steps to forward logs to our Splunk in the doc?
[00:05:20] Daniel: yes, i'll include Splunk forwarding steps and sample config.
[00:05:26] Lena: on contract paperwork, procurement asked whether we can do a short amendment (60 days) that adds uplift and includes a credit for transitioning to Private so costs aren't double-billed.
[00:05:38] Maya: we can draft an amendment with a one-time transition credit. legal prefers to see the timeline, exact node counts, and billing start/stop dates.
[00:05:48] Maya: competitor note — we heard the procurement team benchmarked Anthropic and CloudEndpointX, they were asking about multi-region failover. to be clear, our routing/fallback policy supports region fallback and model variant fallback for continuity.
[00:06:03] Samir: fallback is important — during last incident we saw a regional blip and traffic got rate-limited. how quickly does Redwood fail over?
[00:06:11] Daniel: failover depends on your routing policy; we can set active-active or active-passive. typical failover detection is within 30-90 seconds and you can configure automatic fallback to a lower-cost region.
[00:06:25] Nora: we also need RBAC matrix for admin/devops/dev roles, plus SSO provisioning.
[00:06:33] Maya: we'll include an RBAC sample and SAML mapping doc in the package.
[00:06:39] Lena: great. ok high level next steps and owners?
[00:06:45] Maya: i'll recap at the end but quick owners now: Maya pricing/contract; Daniel test & logs doc; Samir supply traffic; Nora compliance confirmations.
[00:06:55] [Long stretch of technical discussion omitted - 24m of deep technical Q/A on model variants, cache hit ratios, and provisioning windows]
[00:30:50] Daniel: (deep dive) about KV cache: you mentioned lots of prefix reuse — we can enable prefix caching and set a hot-key eviction policy, that will reduce token per inference by up to 30% in your pattern, but depends on session affinity.
[00:31:08] Samir: session affinity is OK, we can maintain session routing for 12h.
[00:31:15] Daniel: perfect — that will help cost during the spike window. also batching config: continuous batching will help throughput if you accept slight p50 increase.
[00:31:30] Lena: acceptable tradeoff.
[00:31:34] [00:31:40] Speaker 2 (unknown): (murmur)
[00:31:44] Maya: circling back, we need the sample and traffic matrix by Friday to start tests next week.
[00:31:50] Samir: we'll push it by EOD Friday.
[00:31:54] Nora: one legal Q — if we extend current term by 60 days, can the uplift be prorated based on actual usage?
[00:31:59] Maya: yes we can do prorated billing for the uplift period, and the amendment will note credits if Private is activated.
[00:32:08] Lena: wrap up — what does the follow-up look like?
[00:32:12] Maya: we'll send: 1) pricing delta sheet and draft amendment; 2) SOC2 & KMS/HSM and SSO docs; 3) Daniel's test plan and sample config for Splunk forwarding; and 4) provisional timeline for EU private cluster activation.
[00:32:27] Daniel: i'll also include example perf numbers from similar customers with similar traffic.
[00:32:33] Nora: thanks, please cc compliance.
[00:32:36] Maya: will do. any final notes?
[00:32:39] Lena: none from me. thanks everyone.
[00:32:43] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with the packet in two business days and the test kick-off after we get traffic.
